language.title: Language
language.label: Interface language
language.description: System follows the OS language. Chinese uses Simplified Chinese.

general.label: General
general.description: The build you are running, how MonoCode reaches you, and the panels it shows.

connections.label: Connections
connections.description: Connect your machines and run agents remotely through SSH.

appearance.label: Appearance
appearance.description: Theme, tint, translucency, workspace layout, and conversation backgrounds.

keybindings.label: Keybindings
keybindings.description: Every shortcut the workspace handles, from the app menu and the key handler.

chat.label: Chat
chat.description: How transcripts read, what the composer does with a follow-up, how files save, and how diffs open.

providers.label: Providers
providers.description: Provider accounts, agent CLIs MonoCode can drive, and the model new sessions start with.

mcp.label: MCP
mcp.description: Find MCP servers across providers and manage their connections.

skills.label: Skills
skills.description: Discover and manage file skills from project, personal, and harness folders.

inbox.label: Inbox
inbox.description: Manage Inbox services and notification preferences for each project.

archive.label: Archive
archive.description: Projects and conversations you have archived.

worktrees.label: Worktrees
worktrees.description: Manage additional worktrees for each project.

monos.label: Monos
monos.description: The resident agent beside your tabs, and which projects have one.

errors.invalid: That combination is not a valid shortcut
errors.activateRange: {{command}} needs a number key from 1 to 8
errors.quickComposerGlobal: Quick Composer needs ⌘ or Ctrl as a global hotkey

keybindings.title: Shortcuts
keybindings.description: Click a shortcut to record new keys. Press Delete while recording to disable it.

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.description: How MonoCode reaches you while you are looking somewhere else.

general.sounds: Short cues for project activity, finished turns, and available updates. Choose project notification categories in Inbox settings. Switches and Copy on a finished turn also play.
general.notifications: Notify when a reminder is due, or when an agent finishes or needs input in another session or while MonoCode is in the background. Click the notification to open that session.

workspace.description: How project navigation and workspace tabs behave.
workspace.title: Workspace

general.file-tabs: Open files beside the active chat, or give each file a normal tab in the top bar. Top-bar files can still be combined into split panes.
general.tab-animations: Animate tabs as they open and close. Turn this off for instant tab changes.
general.notes: A global markdown notebook on the project rail. Save a finished turn from the transcript, then mention it later with @note or add it to chat.
general.quick-composer: Press {{shortcut}} in any app to float a prompt over it and start a session without switching to MonoCode. Change the shortcut in Keybindings. Return starts it in the background; ⌘Return starts it and brings the session forward.
general.working-agents: When two or more chats are in flight, a card on the project rail lists them so you can jump across projects. Finished turns stay until you open that session.
general.close-to-tray: Closing a window hides it to the system tray instead of quitting, so running agents keep going. Reopen from the tray icon, and quit for real from its menu. Turn this off to have close end the window.

transcript.title: Transcript
transcript.description: How a conversation reads as it grows.

chat.transcript-layout: Full width keeps user prompts as a spanning card. Chat aligns them to the right with a max width, like a messaging app.
chat.anchor-prompts: When you send, the new prompt sits at the top of the transcript and the reply grows into the space below. Turn this off to keep the classic layout, with the latest message resting on the composer.

composer.title: Composer
composer.description: What the composer does with what you type.

chat.follow-up: Queue follow-ups until the active turn finishes, or steer the active turn immediately.
chat.model-controls: Show model options beside the picker instead of inside the model menu.

editor.title: Editor
editor.description: What happens when you save a file in the workspace editor.

chat.format-on-save: Run Prettier on supported files before writing. Off keeps the text you typed, including quote style.

codeReview.title: Code review
codeReview.description: Where a turn's changes open when you go to read them.

chat.diff-view: Editor keeps working-tree changes in the file. Unified stacks every changed file in one review, with sticky headers and collapsed unchanged lines.

extras.title: Extras
extras.description: Idle animation, and nothing else. Turn both off for a still workspace.

chat.composer-mascot: When a turn is running, the project mascot runs along the composer, bonks the scroll-to-latest button the first time, then jumps it, and sometimes grabs a coin.
chat.empty-session-games: Pac-man and snake idle on the empty-session grid. Hover the band to take control of whichever is on screen. Turn this off to keep the pane still.

github.description: Pull requests, reviews, and issues, read through the GitHub CLI.
github.connected: GitHub CLI is installed and authenticated. MonoCode uses it for GitHub inbox items.
github.signInHint: Run gh auth login in a terminal, complete the sign-in flow, then check again.
github.installHint: Install GitHub CLI from cli.github.com, run gh auth login in a terminal, then check again.

gitlab.description: Merge requests from GitLab.com or a self-managed instance.
gitlab.connection: Connect GitLab.com or a self-managed GitLab instance. Use a personal access token with API access; the token is stored locally and Disconnect deletes it.

azuredevops.description: Pull requests and Boards work items from your ADO organization.
azuredevops.connection: Connect your ADO organization with a personal access token (Boards + Repos read & write for comments). The token is stored locally and Disconnect deletes it.

jira.description: Jira Cloud issues from the projects you pick.
jira.connectHint: Connect your Jira Cloud site using your Atlassian email and an API token without scopes. Disconnect deletes the saved credentials.
jira.projectsHint: Unchecked projects stay out of the inbox.

linear.description: Issues assigned to you, from the teams you pick.
linear.apiKeyDescription: Create a personal API key in Linear → Settings → Security & Access. Disconnect deletes it.
linear.teamsHint: Unchecked teams stay out of the inbox.

update.idle: MonoCode updates itself from the release feed.

dither.label: Dither
dither.description: Rebuilds the artwork with a dithered color palette.

ascii.label: ASCII
ascii.description: Recreates the artwork with colored characters on black.

halftone.label: Halftone
halftone.description: Recreates the artwork with colored print dots on black.

scanlines.label: Scanlines
scanlines.description: Adds a pronounced horizontal display-line texture.

gradient-blur.label: Haze
gradient-blur.description: Blurs and fades the artwork into the background below.

themeGroup.title: Theme
themeGroup.description: Dark and light share the same tint, so the color settings below apply to both.

appearance.accent-color: Used for the composer send button and your message bubbles.

color.title: Color
color.description: Hue and saturation tint every surface. Lightness only moves the dark theme.

appearance.hue: Base hue for accents and tinted surfaces.
appearance.saturation: How strongly the hue tints the interface. Zero keeps it neutral.
appearance.darkLightnessLight: This only affects dark mode. Your dark-mode value is preserved.
appearance.dark-lightness: Base brightness of the dark theme. Lower values are darker; zero is true black.

translucency.title: Translucency
translucency.light: Light mode always uses an opaque window, so these are off. Your dark-mode values are preserved.
translucency.description: How much of the desktop shows through MonoCode. Blur costs more to composite the higher it goes.

appearance.sidebar-opacity: Applies to the project rail and the other glass panes.
appearance.main-pane-glass: Extend the translucent treatment to the main pane behind sessions and editors.
appearance.collapsed-project-rail: Keep project navigation available as a compact icon rail, or hide the rail completely.
appearance.interface-scale: Zoom the whole interface. You can also use Ctrl+=, Ctrl+-, and Ctrl+0 (Cmd on macOS).
appearance.show-excluded-files: Show files and folders Git excludes, such as build output and dependencies, in the explorer.

chatBackground.description: An image behind your chat panes. It stays on this device.
chatBackground.showOnDescription: Empty sessions only, or every conversation.
chatBackground.emptyVisibilityDescription: Background strength before a chat has messages.
chatBackground.sessionVisibilityDescription: Background strength once the conversation has messages.

appearance.diff-colors: Colors for added and removed lines. Colorblind and High contrast use blue and orange instead of green and red; High contrast adds stronger tints and text.

cli.tooOld: OpenCode v{{version}} is too old. Upgrade to v{{minimum}} or newer.
cli.saveFailed: Could not save the binary path.
cli.pathHint: Enter the absolute path to the CLI executable. Changes apply after restarting MonoCode.
cli.revealFailed: Could not open the CLI location: {{error}}

agentClis.project: These defaults apply to {{project}} only. A provider with Show in picker off is also kept out of new conversations started in this project. CLI paths remain global for MonoCode.
agentClis.global: A provider is listed as installed once its CLI is found on your PATH. Uninstalled CLIs stay listed but are left out of the model picker, as are installed ones with Show in picker off. The model beside a provider is what its new conversations start with; Use by default picks the provider itself. CLI paths are global for MonoCode and apply to every project.

providers.claude-hooks: Run the hooks configured in your settings.json files — PreToolUse command rewrites, blocks, notifications, and the rest — just as the Claude Code CLI would. Turn this off if a hook is misbehaving and you need the session back. Takes effect on the next turn.

accounts.removeConfirm: Remove “{{name}}”? Its stored credentials will be deleted and any running turns for this account will stop. Existing conversations stay in history, but cannot continue until you switch accounts.
accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.description: Create isolated sign-ins for providers that support account profiles. Account switching stays available from the usage control in the footer.
accounts.name: Account name

providers.show-remaining-usage: Fill usage meters with what is left in each limit instead of what has been used.
providers.mask-emails: Blur account emails in Settings and the usage popover until you click one, so they stay out of screenshots.

projects.title: Archived projects
projects.description: Archive a project from the rail to keep its chats without listing it in the sidebar.

sessions.title: Archived conversations
sessions.noProject: Open a project to see its archived conversations.
sessions.empty: No archived conversations in this project.

archive.show-archived: Keep archived conversations listed alongside the active ones.

add.notObject: Configuration must be a JSON object
add.title: Add MCP server
add.description: Paste a server configuration and choose where to add it.
add.name: Name
add.configHint: Paste one entry from an mcpServers block, or a single server object with a name above.

mcp.title: MCP connections
mcp.description: Configured servers for the selected project and your provider accounts.
mcp.empty: No MCP servers configured for this provider.
mcp.footer: Claude Code status comes from its CLI. Other providers show configured entries. Sign in opens your browser when supported.

monos.enabledDescription: Agents of your own on the project rail. Each works on the projects you give it, remembers what matters and picks up habits it runs on its own. Turn this off to hide them.
monos.listDescription: Add one with the plus beside Monos on the rail. Choose its projects from its details.

reset.label: Reset Mono
reset.title: Reset {{name}} to its defaults?
reset.body: Its soul goes back to the default and its name to {{name}}. Changes to its soul can't be recovered.
reset.kept: Its conversation, projects, memory and habits will be kept.
